channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Prazo para tirar ou regularizar título de eleitor termina nesta quarta (06)
item.description: The deadline to obtain a first-time voter ID or regularize an existing one ends this Wednesday (06). Service is available in person at electoral courts or online via the TSE website.

item.title: Não somos um país de desonestos, mas a Copacabana que celebra a latinidade
item.description: The article celebrates Shakira's concert at Copacabana Beach as an affirmation of Latin identity and resistance against conservative agendas that threaten collective interests. The author stresses the need to assert Brazil's cultural and social identity, emphasizing that the country is not defined by dishonesty but by its capacity to celebrate diversity and joy, especially amid social and political crises. References to Zimbabwe's 'friendship benches' mental health initiative and the film 'O Riso e a Faca' reinforce a call for dialogue spaces, mental health support, and overcoming oppression like machismo, linking culture and well-being as pillars of a just society.

item.title: Tarcísio rebate Haddad após crítica à política fiscal de São Paulo: ‘Quebrou o Brasil’
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas rebutted criticisms from former Finance Minister Fernando Haddad regarding the state's fiscal policy, accusing him of having 'broken Brazil' and leaving behind high public debt, elevated interest rates, and widespread delinquency. Tarcísio defended his administration, citing the renegotiation of state debt and asserting that Haddad lacks the moral standing to comment on public finances.

item.title: Como Lula vai ‘desconstruir’ Flávio Bolsonaro, segundo chefe de comunicação do PT
item.description: PT’s national communications secretary, Éden Valadares, says Lula’s campaign must deconstruct Flávio Bolsonaro’s image without using adjectives, presenting only his lifelong hold on public office and lack of work experience. He argues the right will not have a moderate candidate in 2026, as Flávio embodies Bolsonarist continuity, and the notion of a 'third way' does not exist in Brazil.

item.title: Ex-presidente do Credit Suisse que foi de Lula em 2022, é anfitrião de jantar para Flávio Bolsonaro em Miami
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro attended a lengthy dinner in Miami with Brazilian financial sector executives and businesspeople, featuring the former Credit Suisse president who supported Lula in 2022. The event, held last night, brought together influential figures from Brazil’s financial elite and was described as subscriber-only content. The article highlights the growing connection between Bolsonaro’s son and international financial circles, sparking speculation about potential political and economic alliances.

item.title: Diálogo rompido nos bastidores e novos planos para o STF: os impactos da derrota de Lula
item.description: The rejection of Jorge Messias for the Supreme Court by the Senate marked an unprecedented rupture between Lula and Davi Alcolumbre, exposing flaws in government articulation and triggering an institutional impasse. Robson Bonin argues that the president ignored warnings about insufficient votes, turning what was once a formality into a crisis of trust. The mutual silence between the two leaders, without mediation from usual interlocutors, deepens instability and strengthens the Senate’s role in the STF vacancy battle.

item.title: Lula lanza un balón de oxígeno a 28 millones de brasileños endeudados a pocos meses de las elecciones
item.description: Lula launched an aid package for 28 million indebted Brazilians just months ahead of the 2026 elections, responding to declining purchasing power despite strong macroeconomic indicators. The government aims to counter popular dissatisfaction driven by record household debt, which absorbs 30% of family income — the highest in history — even as GDP grows at 3% annually and unemployment hits historic lows. The move is seen as a political lifeline amid eroding government approval.

item.title: Alckmin acredita que encontro entre Lula e Trump será oportunidade para esclarecer funcionamento do PIX
item.description: Vice President Geraldo Alckmin said the meeting between Lula and Trump will be an opportunity to explain how Pix works and seek mutual understanding, emphasizing Brazil is not a problem for the U.S., which has a trade surplus with Brazil. He also commented on the rejection of Jorge Messias for the STF and detailed Novo Desenrola 2.0, a debt renegotiation program allowing partial use of FGTS funds.

item.title: Em pedido a Moraes, general condenado por trama golpista alegou dificuldades financeiras
item.description: Retired General Mario Fernandes, convicted for involvement in the coup plot, requested the STF to allow installment payment of a R$ 64.800 fine in up to 60 monthly installments, citing financial hardship despite earning R$ 23.000 net monthly. He was sentenced to 26 years and six months in prison for drafting a detailed plan to attack authorities, including Lula, Alckmin and Moraes, which included hypotheses of weapon use and poisoning, with the document printed at the Planalto Palace and taken to the Alvorada Palace.

item.title: Manutenção da prisão de Thiago Ávila por Israel é ‘injustificável’, diz Lula
item.description: President Lula criticized Israel's continued detention of Brazilian activist Thiago Ávila as 'unjustifiable,' demanding his immediate release. Ávila was arrested while part of the Global Sumud Flotilla attempting to deliver humanitarian aid to Gaza and is being held in solitary confinement without windows, having started a hunger strike. The Brazilian and Spanish governments jointly condemned the detention as illegal and a violation of international law.

item.title: Lula vai reagir friamente a Alcolumbre após derrota de Messias
item.description: President Lula signaled to allies he intends to react calmly to Davi Alcolumbre following the defeat of Jorge Messias in the Senate, avoiding public retaliation for strategic reasons. Despite being bothered by the alleged agreement involving Alcolumbre, Flávio Bolsonaro, and Alexandre de Moraes, Lula acknowledges he still needs Senate support to advance key agendas like ending the 6×1 work scale.

item.title: Lula exige soltura de brasileiro preso por Israel em flotilha
item.description: President Lula demanded the immediate release of Brazilian activist Thiago Ávila, detained by Israel after the interception of the Global Sumud flotilla in international waters, calling the detention unjustifiable and alleging torture. Lula is working with Spain to secure the freedom of Ávila and Palestinian-Spanish activist Saif Abu Keshek, condemning Israel’s actions as a violation of international law.

item.title: Tarcísio confirma Ramuth como vice e André do Prado ao lado de Derrite ao Senado
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) confirmed that Felício Ramuth (MDB) will remain as his running mate in the re-election bid and that André do Prado (PL), president of the Alesp, will be the second Senate candidate alongside Guilherme Derrite (PP). He also stated that Eduardo Bolsonaro withdrew his Senate candidacy, yielding the spot to André do Prado, and that he does not yet know if Eduardo will serve as his alternate, despite having been invited to the role.

item.title: Lula e Trump devem tratar de minerais críticos e seção 301
item.description: Lula and Trump will meet in Washington on May 6, 2026, to discuss Brazilian rare mineral exploration by U.S. companies, the U.S. Section 301 trade investigation, and cooperation on organized crime. Lula will lead a small delegation including Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira and Justice Minister Wellington César Lima e Silva. The meeting, lasting about an hour, follows a postponement due to the Iran war, with Lula maintaining a protectionist stance on strategic minerals and opposing U.S. designation of Brazilian criminal groups as terrorist organizations.

item.title: Margem do consignado do INSS cairá para 30% até 2031; entenda
item.description: The Lula government is progressively reducing the payroll-deductible loan margin for retirees, pensioners, and public servants from 45% to 30% by 2031, starting with an immediate drop to 40% in May 2026. The policy eliminates exclusive allocations for payroll-deductible credit cards (10% of the total), redirecting that capacity toward lower-interest loans to curb indebtedness. The TCU has ordered an immediate suspension of new payroll-deductible credit card concessions as of April 2026.

item.title: O que aproxima os eleitores de Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The Realtime Big Data poll shows that, despite apparent ideological differences, voters of Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro share similar views on the economy, security, and distrust in institutions, which undermines the expected polarization in the runoff. This convergence suggests the 2026 presidential race may be less ideological and more based on practical assessments of governance and personal trust.

item.title: A ‘desconfiança’ por trás do encontro entre Lula e Trump nos Estados Unidos
item.description: The meeting between Lula and Trump in the U.S. raises distrust due to the lack of prior official confirmation by the United States, which breaks diplomatic protocol and caused concern in the Planalto. Although the Alexandre Ramirez case created recent tensions, it is considered minor compared to key economic agenda items such as rare earths, tariffs, and the Pix system. The meeting could be influenced by Brazil’s electoral context, with risk of an ideological U.S. agenda indirectly benefiting figures like Flávio Bolsonaro, but the outcome will depend on whether the focus remains pragmatic and economic.

item.title: 90% são a favor de maioridade penal em 16 anos, diz pesquisa
item.description: A Real Time Big Data poll reveals that 90% of Brazilians support lowering the age of criminal responsibility to 16, with the highest backing among voters of Flávio Bolsonaro (96%) and Ronaldo Caiado (98%). Among Lula supporters, support stands at 81%. Conducted May 2–4, 2026, with 2,000 respondents, the survey has a 2-point margin of error and is registered with the TSE under BR-03627/2026.

item.title: MP do Novo Desenrola prevê descontos de até 90% em dívidas
item.description: Provisional Measure 1.355/2026 established the Novo Desenrola Brasil, allowing individuals earning up to R$ 8,105 to refinance debts of up to R$ 15,000 per bank, with a maximum interest rate of 1.99% per month and discounts of up to 90%. The program covers credit card, overdraft, personal loan, and FIES debts, with a 90-day window to renegotiate and repayment terms of 12 to 48 months, including the option to use FGTS funds for settlement.

item.title: Procuradoria recorre no TSE e pede que tribunal reconheça cassação de Cláudio Castro
item.description: The Electoral Public Prosecutor's Office (MPE) appealed to the TSE to formally recognize the cassation of Cláudio Castro's diploma, former governor of Rio de Janeiro and PL member. The appeal follows a ruling that stripped him of political rights, with the MPE seeking to enforce the judicial decision. The petition was filed on May 5, 2026.

item.title: Meio-Dia em Brasília: A politização dos tribunais
item.description: The Meio-Dia em Brasília program discussed the politicization of courts such as the STF and TSE, highlighted by public statements from their members. It also covered the launch of the federal government's Desenrola program and the introduction of a new institutional mascot.

item.title: Pode o presidente do Senado se negar a analisar indicação para o STF, aguardando a eleição?
item.description: The Senate President cannot constitutionally withhold a Supreme Court nomination awaiting the 2026 election results, as the Constitution grants the President the power to nominate and the Senate the power to approve, without allowing deliberate obstruction. Delaying the process for political reasons to wait for an election outcome violates Articles 102 and 52, III, 'a' of the 1988 Constitution by undermining the Senate's exclusive prerogative to approve or reject the nominee. There is no constitutional basis for linking STF appointments to electoral outcomes.

item.title: Crusoé: Zema bomba nas redes após treta com Gilmar
item.description: Romeu Zema, the Novo party's presidential pre-candidate, gained nearly 1 million Instagram followers after a public clash with Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes, reaching 3.5 million followers in April. His engagement rate doubled from 2.34% to 4.55%, signaling a significant boost in his social media visibility.

item.title: Governo acaba com cartão consignado do INSS no novo Desenrola
item.description: The federal government announced the termination of the INSS payroll loan card as part of the new Desenrola Brasil program, designed to renegotiate debts and support President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s re-election bid. The measure, disclosed on Monday (4), eliminates a credit line used by retirees and pensioners, raising concerns among beneficiaries. Desenrola Brasil is positioned as a key driver for Lula’s 2026 electoral campaign.

item.title: A confiança dos eleitores nas instituições, segundo nova pesquisa
item.description: A Real Time Big Data poll shows low voter confidence in Brazilian institutions, with the Armed Forces being the most trusted at 48%, followed by the press at 40%, the Supreme Federal Court at 36%, and the National Congress at 32%. The survey interviewed 2,000 people between May 2 and 4, 2026, with a margin of error of two percentage points.

item.title: Em crise com Alcolumbre, Lula quer virar a página após derrota acachapante no Senado
item.description: Following the Senate's rejection of Jorge Messias' nomination, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva urged his government and congressional allies to 'turn the page' and avoid holding grudges against the Legislative leadership, particularly Senate President Davi Alcolumbre. Lula acknowledged the strain in his relationship with Alcolumbre but instructed Institutional Relations Minister José Guimarães and Government Leader Randolfe Rodrigues to maintain constructive dialogue with the Amapá senator, whose support remains vital for advancing executive priorities. He also called on government officials who have experienced tensions with Alcolumbre to work toward rebuilding bridges.

item.title: NOVA PESQUISA BIG DATA PRESIDENTE 1º E 2º TURNO ! MAIO 2026 LULA X FLÁVIO: quem está na FRENTE ?
item.description: The Big Data poll from May 2026 shows Flávio Bolsonaro leading Lula in the first round with a significant advantage. In the second-round scenario, the gap remains stable, indicating a consolidation of support for the opposition candidate. The results suggest a potential political shift in Brazil, though margin of error and electoral volatility should be taken into account.

item.title: Pesquisas eleitorais: as armas de Lula e Flávio que podem mudar o jogo, segundo diretor do Real Time Big Data
item.description: A Real Time Big Data poll shows Lula at 40% and Flávio Bolsonaro at 34% in the first round, with Lula leading due to left-wing vote concentration. In the second-round simulation, they are technically tied: Flávio at 44% and Lula at 43%, as fragmented right-wing voters (Caiado, Zema, Renan Santos) shift toward the senator. Both candidates face high rejection (Lula 44%, Flávio 41%), and the economy remains the central voter concern.

item.title: Câmara volta a pautar programa de escolas cívico-militares encerrado pelo MEC
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies will resume debate on the National Civic-Military Schools Program this Wednesday (6), with a vote scheduled in the Committee on Foreign Relations and National Defense. The bill, authored by Deputy Captain Alberto Neto (PL-AM), aims to reinstate the program terminated by the Ministry of Education in 2023, which involved military police and firefighters in basic education schools. While supporters claim it improves educational quality, President Lula has publicly criticized the model, stating Brazil does not need its expansion, and researchers warn of risks including salary disparities and harm to child development.

item.title: Flávio e Valdemar se reúnem com empresários brasileiros em Miami
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for presidency, met with Brazilian businessmen in Miami at the home of Marcelo Kayath, with the participation of PL president Valdemar Costa Neto. The meeting, part of a series of dialogues with the market following his improved polling numbers, focused on discussing his economic policy, fiscal commitment, and relations with investors, referencing his father’s government as a model while emphasizing that a potential term would not repeat the pandemic context. The outreach to the economic establishment signals an effort to reduce uncertainties and build bridges with the productive sector amid an still-open electoral scenario.

item.title: André do Prado volta aos EUA para definir últimos detalhes e ser anunciado por Eduardo Bolsonaro como candidato ao Senado por SP
item.description: State deputy André do Prado (PL) returned to the United States to finalize details of his Senate candidacy in São Paulo with Eduardo Bolsonaro (PL), who will serve as his alternate and is expected to announce the candidacy later this week. The move aligns with Governor Tarcísio de Freitas’s (Republicans) strategy to field a center-right candidate to counter left-wing leads in polls, while federal deputy Guilherme Derrite (PP-SP) is also set to be announced as a right-wing Senate candidate next week.

item.title: MP Eleitoral vê contradição do TSE e pede cassação de diploma de Castro
item.description: The Electoral Public Prosecutor's Office filed appeals with the TSE, pointing to a contradiction in the ruling that acquitted former Rio de Janeiro governor Cláudio Castro (PL) of political and economic power abuse in the 2022 elections. The MP claims the decision contains inconsistencies that undermine its validity and is seeking the annulment of Castro's diploma. The case highlights tensions between the Electoral MP and the TSE regarding the application of the clean slate law.

item.title: Governistas admitem que PEC da Segurança não deve avançar neste ano e querem foco em fim da escala 6x1
item.description: Governist senators admit the Public Security PEC will not advance before October due to lack of Senate action and President Davi Alcolumbre’s evasive stance. The government is now prioritizing popular appeals like ending the 6x1 work scale, following the political fallout from the Messias rejection and Alcolumbre’s growing independence in the chamber.

item.title: Câmara vota projeto que amplia controle do governo sobre minerais estratégicos
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies is set to vote on Tuesday, April 5, on a bill establishing the National Policy on Critical and Strategic Minerals, expanding federal government control over exploration and commercialization of these resources. The bill creates the Critical and Strategic Minerals Committee (CMCE), with authority to veto mergers, block foreign direct investment, and restrict low-value-added exports. Prioritized by the Lula administration, the initiative aims to safeguard national strategic interests amid global competition for lithium, nickel, and rare earths — key inputs for clean energy technologies and electric vehicles.

item.title: Pesquisa: o que o brasileiro pensa sobre reduzir a maioridade penal para 16 anos
item.description: A Real Time Big Data survey shows 90% of Brazilians support reducing the age of criminal responsibility from 18 to 16, with only 8% opposed and 2% undecided. Support is widespread across voters of all major 2026 presidential candidates, ranging from 81% among Lula (PT) supporters to 98% among Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) backers. Though historically opposed by the left, the issue now displays broad transpartisan consensus despite traditional ideological divides.

item.title: Congresso comunica ao governo derrubada do veto ao PL da Dosimetria
item.description: Congress formally notified the government that it overturned President Lula’s veto on the Dosimetria Bill, which reduces penalties for those convicted of the January 8 attacks. The president now has 48 hours to promulgate the law, as required by constitutional procedure. The move marks a political setback for the Executive and a victory for lawmakers aligned with those accused of the coup attempt.

item.title: Gleisi Hoffmann comenta sobre Alcolumbre e diz que governo 'não pode ter inimigo dentro de casa'
item.description: Federal Deputy Gleisi Hoffmann (PT-PR) criticized Senate President Davi Alcolumbre (União Brasil-AP), stating the government cannot have an 'enemy within'. She emphasized the need for internal unity in the Executive to avoid political wear and tear.

item.title: Flávio faz bate e volta aos EUA às vésperas da reunião entre Lula e Trump
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro traveled to the U.S. shortly before the Lula-Trump meeting, on a trip described as a political or cultural mission, and was seen with his brother Eduardo Bolsonaro wearing a shirt featuring the Bolsonaro family. Prior to departure, he attended a church service with pastor Silas Malafaia following public disagreements over the PL presidential nomination. According to Real Time Big Data, Lula leads in the first round with 40% versus Flávio’s 34%, while a potential second round shows a technical tie at 44% to 43%.

item.title: Grupo de Flávio Bolsonaro articula obstrução no Congresso e ajuda de Alcolumbre por sucessão no Rio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's group is coordinating congressional obstruction with Davi Alcolumbre's support to secure Rio de Janeiro's succession, aiming to install Douglas Ruas as interim PL governor ahead of the October elections. The strategy includes pressuring the STF and leveraging the institutional authority of Chamber and Senate presidents to remove Ricardo Couto from Guanabara Palace and strengthen the Bolsonarist electoral base.

item.title: Pagamento de obra com crédito tributário e valor de multa segue para a Câmara
item.description: The Economic Affairs Committee (CAE) approved Bill 1.252/2023, allowing the Union, states, Federal District, and municipalities to pay for engineering works and services through tax credits or settlement of administrative fines, without direct use of budgetary resources. The bill sets limits of up to R$2 million or 2% of the entity’s current net revenue, requires public interest evaluation by a committee, permits use in public-private partnerships (PPPs), and includes transparency and sanction rules. As the decision is terminative, the text now proceeds to the Chamber of Deputies unless a plenary vote is requested.

item.title: TSE gastará R$ 1,3 milhão com Photoshop e afins
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) will spend approximately R$1.3 million on the hiring and renewal of licenses for audiovisual production, graphic design, and engineering software, with a 36-month validity. The expenditure is part of a campaign to improve the image of the Brazilian Justice System and strengthen confidence in the electronic voting machine.

item.title: TSE lança 'Pilili', mascote oficial das urnas eletrônicas no Brasil
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) unveiled the mascot Pilili to celebrate 30 years of electronic voting in Brazil. The name references the sound made by the voting machine when confirming a vote. The initiative aims to make the electoral process more accessible and playful for the public.

item.title: TSE apresenta Pilili, mascote sem gênero das eleições de 2026
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) unveiled Pilili as the official mascot for the 2026 Brazilian elections, inspired by the 30-year-old electronic voting machine. Pilili is a gender-neutral character symbolizing democratic neutrality and will travel across the country to promote civic participation in voting. TSE President Minister Cármen Lúcia emphasized that the electronic voting system has eliminated fraud and ensured that each vote reflects solely the voter’s choice.

item.title: Cármen Lúcia será a relatora de ação penal contra Moro por calúnia a Gilmar
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Cármen Lúcia will be the rapporteur of the criminal action against Senator Sergio Moro for alleged slander against Justice Gilmar Mendes. The accusation stems from a video in which Moro mocked Mendes at a June party, implying he was taking bribes to grant habeas corpus. In March, the First Chamber unanimously rejected Moro’s appeal against the acceptance of the indictment.

item.title: Conselho de Ética vota suspensão de Van Hattem e mais 2 deputados
item.description: The Ethics Committee of the Chamber of Deputies is voting on Tuesday (May 5) on a report recommending a two-month suspension of the mandates of deputies Marcel Van Hattem (Novo-RS), Marcos Pollon (PL-MS), and Zé Trovão (PL-SC) for occupying the Director's Table in August 2025 during a protest against the house arrest of Jair Bolsonaro. The rapporteur, Moses Rodrigues (União Brasil-CE), argues the measure is necessary to make clear that Parliament will not tolerate conduct that obstructs the legislative process. Van Hattem labeled the process an 'endless persecution' and vowed to defend his mandate through mobilization.

item.title: Esquerda aciona MPT contra Romeu Zema por fala sobre ‘trabalho infantil’
item.description: Túlio Gadelha (PSD-PE), president of the Mixed Parliamentary Front for the Eradication of Child Labor, filed a complaint with the Labor Public Ministry (MPT) against Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and presidential pre-candidate, after Zema advocated for relaxing child labor laws in Brazil. Zema’s remarks suggesting children could work under certain conditions provoked strong backlash from left-wing groups and lawmakers. The MPT will investigate potential violations of labor laws and children's rights statutes.

item.title: Associação vê propaganda eleitoral antecipada em culto de Malafaia e pede inelegibilidade de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Pastor Silas Malafaia endorsed Flávio Bolsonaro’s 2026 presidential pre-candidacy during a religious service at ADVEC, interrupting liturgy to invite politicians to the altar and lead a collective prayer. The Secular Brazil Movement filed a complaint with the Rio de Janeiro Regional Electoral Prosecutor’s Office, alleging early electioneering, abuse of religious and economic power, and requesting eight years of ineligibility for Malafaia and Bolsonaro, fines, and annulment of candidacy registrations.

item.title: Líderes da oposição apostam que Alcolumbre irá barrar indicação de novo ministro do STF
item.description: Opposition leaders aim to delay the appointment of a new STF minister until after the 2026 elections, following the rejection of Jorge Messias. They acknowledge that Lula’s potential nomination of a Black female jurist with impeccable reputation would create a dilemma, as rejecting her would give the government campaign ammunition. Thus, they hope Senate President Davi Alcolumbre will block the nomination by not scheduling the hearing, taking the political heat in exchange for expected support from Flávio Bolsonaro for his Senate re-election.

item.title: Lula acerta ao lançar 'Desenrola 2.0', mas ainda não fez acenos na direção ao Centro, alertam aliados
item.description: President Lula got it right launching 'Desenrola 2.0', which relieves indebted Brazilians and supports the economy, but allies warn he is not reaching out to centrist voters. They fear his anti-system rhetoric, as in his Workers' Day speech, may alienate decisive independent voters. The strategy focuses first on reconquering his base before targeting the center.

item.title: Master: Enquanto todo mundo fala, a PF trabalha
item.description: While public discourse is dominated by narratives of conspiracy, smoke screens, and competing versions, the Federal Police continue operating silently in investigations that could shape the future of Lula’s third term. The central question is not whether political rhetoric is right or wrong, but whether PF operations will lead to real political consequences — or if this is merely another round of musical chairs. The end of Lula 3 is not yet determined, but the weight of ongoing inquiries suggests we are at a moment of decision, not spectacle.
